passage: Note from Sonali, school counsellor. Mehak came to see me on Monday after reading that the author she admired most had been found to have copied parts of another writer's book. She said, "Everything I believed is fake," and told me she had torn her poster off the wall that morning. She was shaking a little. I did not tell her to stop being upset. I asked which ideas of the author she still thought were true, and she named the essays on patience and starting again. We talked about how ideas can stand on their own even when a person disappoints us. By Thursday the poster was in a drawer, but the book was back on her desk.

qa.q: Where did the poster end up by Thursday?
qa.a: The poster was in a drawer, and the book was back on her desk.

qa.q: What was Mehak feeling when she said everything she believed was fake?
qa.a: She felt crushed and let down, since her admiration for the author had felt like part of what she believed.

qa.q: How could Mehak keep what is good in the author's ideas?
qa.a: She can judge each essay on its own merits, keep the ones that still make sense, and admire people without expecting them to be perfect.

qa.q: How might Sonali see Mehak's reaction?
qa.a: As a normal part of growing up, since the disappointment shows how much Mehak cared, and Sonali guided Mehak instead of dismissing it.

grounding: A teen is crushed when an admired author turns out to be flawed and learns to keep the ideas but drop the idolisation.

passage:
Thursday night
I can't believe it. Dolma sent me the article at lunch: Meher Qadir, the climate speaker I've followed for two years, copied big parts of her famous river speech from a college student's blog. She even admitted it. I felt like someone punched me. Her quote is stuck above my desk. I was so upset I didn't eat dinner, and Ammi thought I was ill.
But after dinner I looked at the jute bag I made, and the neem saplings on our balcony. Meher didn't grow those. I did. The ideas still work even if she's not perfect. Tomorrow I'm replacing her quote with one from the student she copied.
Zeenat

qa.a: She copied big parts of her famous river speech from a college student's blog.

qa.q: What was Zeenat feeling after reading the article Dolma sent?
qa.a: Zeenat felt crushed and upset, as if punched, because the speaker followed for two years had copied.

qa.q: How did Zeenat keep the ideas while dropping the idolisation?
qa.a: Zeenat focused on the jute bag and neem saplings Zeenat made, and chose to honour the student who was copied.

qa.q: How might Ammi have seen Zeenat skipping dinner?
qa.a: Ammi thought Zeenat was ill, not knowing the upset came from losing faith in a hero.

grounding: Illustrates a teen crushed when an admired speaker proves flawed, keeping the ideas while letting go of the idolisation.

passage:
Wasim: have u seen the old posts of Kabir Rana
Neelam: the chess guy? yeah it's everywhere
Wasim: he mocked a kid in a wheelchair. years ago. I feel sick
Wasim: I literally have his poster. I learned the London opening from his videos
Neelam: that's awful. u ok?
Wasim: no. feels like the whole thing was fake
Neelam: the opening still works tho. u won the district rapid with it
Wasim: 😔 yeah
Neelam: keep the chess. drop the poster
Wasim: maybe I'll find someone else to learn endgames from. someone actually kind
Neelam: or just learn from lots of people. no more one hero
Wasim: deal 👍

qa.q: Which opening did Wasim learn from Kabir Rana's videos?
qa.a: Wasim learned the London opening from his videos.

qa.q: What was Wasim feeling after seeing the old posts?
qa.a: Wasim felt sick and crushed, as if the admiration had all been fake.

qa.q: What did Neelam suggest, and why is it wise?
qa.a: Keep the chess and drop the poster, learning from lots of people, so Wasim keeps the useful ideas without worshipping one flawed hero.

qa.q: How might Neelam feel watching a friend be crushed?
qa.a: Neelam seems concerned and caring, asking if Wasim is okay before helping sort out what to keep.

grounding: Shows a teen crushed by an idol's old cruelty, and a friend helping keep the skills learned while dropping the hero worship.
